text:
Marie L: quick heads-up, saw a latency regression on the rw-13b-int8 canary this morning. P50 jumped ~35% for batch sizes 8-16. kicking off nsys capture now.

PerfBot: [regression alert] service=hosted-infer route=/v1/generate delta_p50=+34.9% :rotating_light:

Alex G: ouch. can you share the trace when its up? want to check for memcpy storms or unexpected kernels.

Marie L: uploaded nsys -> perfetto: https://perfetto.redwood/p/1936002467. capture command: `nsys profile -o /tmp/rw-canary-1936002467 --trace=cuda,osrt --stats=true --capture-range=kernel --duration=150`. short summary: kernel timeline shows flips between our int8_fused_gemm and cudnn_conv at certain steps. also many small H2D copies before decoder.

Devin R: skimmed the trace. the cudnn_conv spikes line up with seq_len jumps (samples at ~560-640). when cudnn path is taken we see an extra dequant + host staging step. looks like KV cache accesses are non-contiguous which forces staging.

Lia P: is cudnn choosing a different algo because of workspace constraints, or because of shape? cudnn often picks different conv algos for tall-skinny arrays.

Marie L: stack around kernel selection in runtime:
```
choose_kernel(model, seqlen, batch) {
  if (quant==INT8 && seqlen <= 512 && batch <= 12) return int8_fused_gemm;
  if (seqlen > 512 && has_cudnn && !force_our_gemm) return cudnn_conv;
  return int8_dequant_gemm;
}
```
This explains the threshold behavior. runtime then performs layout transform for cudnn which currently materializes on host for our strided KV layout.

Alex G: so two problems: selector flips to cudnn for >512, and layout transform triggers host->device memcpy storm.

Devin R: repro plan: 1) microbench seq_len sweep (256,384,512,640,768,1024) measuring P50/P95 and kernel timelines; 2) KV access microtest to log memcpy sizes and counts; 3) try `force_our_gemm=true` to confirm perf delta.

Marie L: ran a quick forced-gemm canary toggle. with `force_our_gemm=true` P50 returned to baseline. performing an autotune probe next to see if cudnn can ever beat our kernel for those shapes.

Lia P: long-term fixes: (a) extend selector to do cheap autotune/probe per shape (workspace-aware), (b) implement contiguous KV compaction path in runtime to avoid host staging for cudnn path, (c) add CI perf test sweeping seq_lens to catch regressions.

Alex G: short-term mitigation: set `force_our_gemm=true` for canary and adjust batch-splitting heuristic to prefer micro-batches when latency is critical. also accepting KV compaction PR if its small.

Devin R: Ill run the autotune probe and post a table of throughput/wspace for each shape by EOD. will also attach short nsys captures for 384/512/768/1024.

PerfBot: action created: PERF-3892 "int8 cudnn-fallback on seq_len spike" assigned to Marie L priority=P1

SRE-Bot: deploy note: forced-gemm toggle rolled to canary at 1936002600 UTC (scope: rw-13b-int8). monitoring metrics.

Marie L: thanks all. will open PR for KV compaction (small buffer transform + unit test), upload microbench CSVs and attach nsys captures to PERF-3892. closing loop once autotune + KV patch merged.

Alex G: good catch. once autotune lands we should consider a background profiler that updates selector heuristics on real traffic shapes.

Lia P: agreed. adding a perf-regression CI job that runs lightweight traces across seq_lens and verifies kernel choices.

Marie L: ack, will update the ticket with traces and timelines later today.
